records.originHebrew: וְאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (יג.): כָּל הַכּוֹפֵר בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נִקְרָא "יְהוּדִי", לָכֵן אָמְרוּ שָׁם בְּיוֹמָא דְּגַם בּוֹ נֶאֱמַר: "יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי" (תְּהִלִּים ס, ט), רַק דְּלָא מַסִּיק וְכוּלֵי. דְּוַדַּאי הַמִּשְׁפָּט מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה: הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לוֹ סְתָרָיו, אֶלָּא דְּזֶה אֵינוֹ אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא, פֵּירוּשׁ לְשׁוֹן "הֲלָכָה" הַיְינוּ מִלְּשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב "זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, כא). וּלְעִנְיַן הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם אָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (נט:): "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא", וְאֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּבַת קוֹל; (וְשָׁם פו.) נֶחְלְקוּ בִּמְתִיבְתָּא דִּרְקִיעָא: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹמֵר וְכוּלֵי, כִּי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם נִקְרָא: חֻקָּה חָקַקְתִּי, גְּזֵירָה גָּזַרְתִּי וְכוּלֵי. וְכֵן הַבְּרִיאָה דְּהוּא מַעֲשֵׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא "חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ", וְכֵן "יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי" נִתְגַּלּוּ לוֹ חוּקּוֹת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא;
records.originEnglish: They said in Megillah: anyone who rejects idolatry is called a Jew. Therefore they said there in Yoma that “Judah is My lawgiver” applies to him too, except that he does not bring the discussion to its conclusion. Certainly the judgment is measure for measure: God reveals His secrets to him. But this is not the halakhic conclusion. The word halakhah comes from “This is the way; walk in it.” Concerning the conduct of the world they said, “It is not in Heaven,” and a heavenly voice is not taken into account. Elsewhere, the heavenly academy disputes a matter, and the Holy One, blessed be He, says one view. Written Torah, which comes from Heaven, is called “I have enacted a statute; I have issued a decree.” Creation, God’s work, is likewise called “the statutes of heaven and earth.” Similarly, “Judah is My lawgiver” means that the statutes of the Holy One, blessed be He, were revealed to him.
records.targetHebrew: דְּדֶגֶל הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל מַחֲנֵה יְהוּדָה, וְהוּא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, דִּכְתִיב: "יְהוּדָה מְחֹקְקִי", וְאַף שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא כ״ו עַמּוּד א׳) דְּלָא מַסִּיק שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִקַּר שֹׁרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא מִשֵּׁבֶט יְהוּדָה; וּמַה דְּלָא מַסִּיק שְׁמַעְתָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהִלְכְתָא הוּא מֵחֲמַת גֹּדֶל הָעֹמֶק וְאֵין יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמֹד עַל סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל רַבִּי מֵאִיר; וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם סְתָם מִשְׁנָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְנִקְרָא "רַבִּי מֵאִיר" שֶׁהוּא מֵאִיר עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים בַּהֲלָכָה.
records.targetEnglish: The first banner, that of the camp of Judah, is the root of Oral Torah, as it says, “Judah is My lawgiver.” Although they said that he does not bring the discussion to its halakhic conclusion, the principal root of Oral Torah nevertheless comes from the tribe of Judah. His not bringing the discussion to its halakhic conclusion is because of its great depth, which others cannot fully fathom, as they said concerning Rabbi Meir. Nevertheless, an anonymous Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir, and he is called Rabbi Meir because he illuminates the sages’ eyes in halakhah.
records.themeTitle: A teaching can illuminate halakhah without itself settling the ruling
records.themeSummary: The example of Rabbi Meir explains how an unusually deep root of Torah can contribute decisively even when others cannot follow it to a practical conclusion.
records.explanation: Chanukah compares Yehudah’s depth to Rabbi Meir: the inability to determine the final ruling from his discussion does not mean his Torah lacks illumination for the sages. This clarifies the distinction the present siman draws between an insight into divine decrees and the practical ‘way in which to walk.’ Both can be Torah, but they play different roles. Revealed depth does not dispense with the processes through which a ruling becomes authoritative in practice.

records.originHebrew: וְרוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן טָב בְּכָל סִטְרִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קפב עַמּוּד ב), וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית (ד.): דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּקָא מְרַתְּחָא, פֵּירוּשׁ: כְּשֶׁהַכַּעַס הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהַתּוֹרָה מַרְתִּיחָתוֹ, שֶׁעַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה רָאוּי לִכְעוֹס, כְּעִנְיַן הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁדָּנוּ נְפָשׁוֹת, וְאֵין מְמַנִּין בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין זָקֵן וְכוּלֵי (סַנְהֶדְרִין לו:), שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ מְלֵאִים רַחֲמִים בֶּאֱמֶת וּמִשְׁתַּדְּלִים לִמְצוֹא זְכוּת עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה, וּרְתִיחָתָם רַק מִצַּד הֶכְרֵחַ הַתּוֹרָה זֶה נִקְרָא רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנָן, הָאוֹהֲבֵי הַתּוֹרָה בֶּאֱמֶת, שֶׁגַּם בְּעֵת כַּעֲסוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִצַּד הַתּוֹרָה וְזוֹכֵר וּמִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים. וְהָעֲצִירָה בְּעֵת הַכַּעַס הוּא אַהֲבָה "בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ",
records.originEnglish: “The anger of the sages is good on every side,” as the Zohar says. This is the Gemara’s statement that Torah is what heats him: the anger is only what Torah causes, when according to Torah it is fitting to become angry. The example is the Sanhedrin judging capital cases, concerning which it says that an elderly person is not appointed to the Sanhedrin. They were truly full of mercy and strove to find grounds for acquittal according to Torah; their heat came only from Torah’s necessity. This is called the anger of sages who truly love Torah: even during anger it is only on Torah’s account, and they remember and strive for mercy. Restraint at the time of anger is love “with all your soul.”
records.targetHebrew: וְהָעִנְיָן, דְּבֶאֱמֶת שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא אֵשׁ כַּעַס, וּכְמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַחֲמָתוֹ בָּעֲרָה בוֹ", וְרוֹצֶה לִשְׂרֹף וּלְכַלּוֹת הַכֹּל; אֲבָל לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה לְתַקֵּן הַרְבֵּה כַּעַס, וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן אֵשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ד׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "הַאי צוּרְבָא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּרָתַח אוֹרַיְּתָא הוּא דְּקָא מַרְתְּחָא לֵיהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ'"; וְהוּא אֵשׁ אוֹכְלָה אֵשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁשּׂוֹרֵף וּמְכַלֶּה אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע; וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב׳ קפ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): "רוּגְזָא דְּרַבָּנַן טָב אִיהוּ לְכָל סִטְרִין וְכוּלֵיהּ".
records.targetEnglish: The root of the evil inclination is the fire of anger, as in “His fury burned within him”; it wishes to burn and consume everything. Corresponding to this in holiness is Oral Torah: much wisdom to repair much anger. It too is fire, as the Gemara says: “When a Torah scholar grows heated, Torah is what heats him, as it is written, ‘Are not My words like fire?’” It is a fire consuming the fire of the evil inclination, burning and consuming that inclination. This is why the Zohar says, “The anger of the sages is good on every side.”
records.themeTitle: The test of Torah’s fire is that it consumes the inclination’s destructive anger
records.themeSummary: Kislev distinguishes a fire that seeks to destroy everything from Oral Torah’s wisdom, which repairs that very anger.
records.explanation: The Kislev passage explains what distinguishes two outwardly similar intensities: the inclination’s fire consumes indiscriminately, while Torah’s fire is directed against the inclination itself. This sharpens the test given here for the anger of a talmid chacham. The Sanhedrin’s search for merit and continuing compassion are not exceptions to holy zeal; they show that the heat remains governed by Torah rather than by personal aggression. Self-restraint therefore expresses love ‘with all your soul.’

records.originHebrew: וְהַחֲלוֹם שֶׁבְּעֵת הַשֵּׁינָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּיָדוֹ וּבְחִירָתוֹ לְנַקּוֹת הִרְהוּרָיו, וְכֵן הִרְהוּרֵי וְדִמְיוֹנוֹת כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל זְמַן שֶׁהֵם דּוּגְמַת חֲלוֹם, הֵם אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַמְדַמֶּה שֶׁהִיא נְבוּאָה. כִּי גַּם בָּהֶם מְלוּבָּשׁ פִּתְרוֹן הָאֲמִיתִּי וּמְרוּמָּז חָכְמַת אֱמֶת הַנִּמְשָׁכוֹת מֵחַבַּ"ד שֶׁבְּמוֹחוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁמְּעוּרְבָּב בְּבַטָּלָה הַרְבֵּה, כְּעִנְיַן "אֵין חֲלוֹם בְּלֹא דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים" (בְּרָכוֹת נה.). וּבְלִקּוּטֵי תּוֹרָה פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב בֵּיאֵר עִנְיַן הַחֲלוֹם: מוֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ מוֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת, עַיֵּין שָׁם. וְכֵן הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל הֶבֶל הֵם מוֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּתוֹ; וְאֵצֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ אֱמֶת וְאֵינָהּ דִּמְיוֹן, הֲרֵי הַמּוֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת גָּנוּז תּוֹךְ מוֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת. רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִפְּנֵי הַקַּטְנוּת הַמְסַבְּבוֹ אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא דָּבָר בָּטֵל, אֲבָל יֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם בָּר. וְהַמֵּבִין עַל זֶה לָדַעַת הַתּוֹכִיּוּת שֶׁבְּכָל הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת הוּא מִי שֶׁנָּקִי מִתַּאֲווֹת, כְּיוֹסֵף בְּתַאֲוַת נָשִׁים וְדָנִיֵּאל בְּתַאֲוַת אֲכִילָה – הֵם הָיוּ פּוֹתְרֵי חֲלוֹמוֹת; דְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הִרְהוּרֵי בַּטָּלָה הֵם בַּתַּאֲווֹת שֶׁבָּזֶה הַלֵּב חוֹשֵׁק לְהַרְהֵר. וּמִי שֶׁהוּא שָׁקוּעַ בַּדִּמְיוֹן אֵין יָכוֹל לְהַחֲלִיף וּלְהוֹצִיא הַדְּבַר אֱמֶת הַמְלוּבָּשׁ תּוֹךְ הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת; רַק מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁקוּעַ הוּא יוּכַל לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב מִן הָרָע.
records.originEnglish: A dream during sleep, when it is not in one’s power or choice to purify one’s thoughts—and likewise the thoughts and imaginings of every Israelite that resemble a dream—is one-sixtieth of the truth of the imaginative faculty, namely prophecy. A true interpretation is clothed even in these, and true wisdom proceeding from the mind’s wisdom, understanding, and knowledge is hinted within them. Yet much that is empty is mixed in, in accordance with “There is no dream without idle elements.” In Likkutei Torah on Vayeshev, a dream is explained as expanded consciousness within contracted consciousness. Idle imaginings similarly belong to contracted consciousness. In Israel, each of whom has a root in Torah, which is truth and not imagination, expanded consciousness is hidden within contracted consciousness. Still, because the smallness surrounds it, there must be an idle element, although there is also grain within it. The one able to understand the inner content of all these imaginings is someone free of desires: Joseph in the desire for women, and Daniel in the desire for food, were interpreters of dreams. The root of idle thoughts is in desires about which the heart wishes to think. Someone immersed in imagination cannot exchange and extract the true matter clothed within those imaginings. Someone not immersed in it can separate the good from the evil.
records.targetHebrew: וְכֵן הַשֵּׁינָה, שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים לְמִיתָה, גַּם כֵּן לְתוֹעֶלֶת זֶה: שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג בְּשֵׁינָה מַה שֶּׁלֹּא יוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג בְּהָקִיץ בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ עַל הָאֲרִיזַ"ל שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר: שֶׁקִּבֵּל וְהִשִּׂיג בְּשֵׁינָה בְּשַׁבָּת בְּפָרָשַׁת בָּלָק מַה שֶּׁלֹּא יוּכַל לִדְרֹשׁ שְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה; וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא: "חֲלוֹם אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים לִנְבוּאָה", וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה: "נוֹבְלוֹת נְבוּאָה חֲלוֹם".
records.targetEnglish: Sleep, which is one-sixtieth of death, can serve the same purpose: a person can attain in sleep what he could not possibly attain while awake. Thus it is written of the Ari that on one occasion he said he had received and attained in his sleep on Shabbat, concerning the portion of Balak, what he could not expound in eighty years. This accords with the Talmud’s saying that a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy, and the Midrash’s saying that a dream is an offshoot of prophecy.
records.themeTitle: An inward insight during sleep still requires discernment of its mixture
records.themeSummary: Kislev explains the possibility of attaining something in sleep that is unavailable while awake; this siman explains the conditions for separating its truth from imagination.
records.explanation: The report about the Ari illustrates why sleep need not be spiritual emptiness. Read with this siman, however, the possibility of hidden wisdom does not certify every dream or passing image. Tzidkat HaTzadik explicitly retains the mixture of idle material and explains the purity from personal desires required for interpretation. The two passages distinguish the presence of a hidden content from a person’s ability to identify that content faithfully.

records.originHebrew: וְהֲגַם דְּכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ זְמַן שֶׁהוּא בְּקַטְנוּת וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת לְעוֹלָם בְּגַדְלוּת וּדְבֵיקוּת הָרָאוּי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת הַשֵּׁינָה וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ט) שֶׁהוּא "טוֹב מְאֹד", שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִינּוֹחַ וְחוֹזֵר לְקַבֵּל חַיּוּת חָדָשׁ, וְכֵן צָרִיךְ לִינּוֹחַ מְעַט מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לִפְעָמִים, וּ"בִיטּוּלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה זֶהוּ יְסוּדָהּ" (מְנָחוֹת צט:), מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן יֵשׁ חִלּוּק בֵּין הִרְהוּרִים כְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁעַל לִבּוֹ. וּכְעִנְיַן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, חֲלוֹמוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ בְּעֵת הַקַּטְנוּת הוּא גַּם כֵּן: "וְהִנֵּה ה' נִצָּב עָלָיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יג), וְכֵן כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ.
records.originEnglish: Although everyone has a time of diminished consciousness, and it is impossible to remain always in expanded consciousness and the proper cleaving to God—as sleep was created and Bereshit Rabbah calls it ‘very good,’ because through it one rests and returns to receive fresh vitality—so too one must sometimes rest a little from words of Torah, and ‘the suspension of Torah is its foundation.’ Nevertheless, even at such a time, a person’s thoughts differ according to his level in the Torah that is upon his heart. Thus with our father Jacob: his dream, the images he experienced at the time of diminished consciousness, was also ‘Behold, the Lord stood over him.’ So it is with each person according to his level.
records.targetHebrew: וְאִיתָא גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): "'וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד' – טוֹבָה שֵׁינָה, וְכִי שֵׁינָה טוֹב מְאֹד וְכוּלֵי? אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּא יָשֵׁן קִימְעָא הוּא עוֹמֵד וְיָגֵעַ בַּתּוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה". וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּתַקֵּן הַנְּפִילָה עַצְמָהּ שֶׁתְּהֵא לוֹ סַיַּיעְתָּא לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִמֶּנָּה יִקַּח לַעֲבוֹד אֶת הַשֵּׁם. וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ בְּחֹדֶשׁ כִּסְלֵו: "הִמְלִיךְ אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ בְּשֵׁינָה וְכִסְלֵו בַּשָּׁנָה".
records.targetEnglish: In Bereshit Rabbah it is taught: ‘Behold, it was very good’—this is sleep. They ask: is sleep very good? Rather, through sleeping a little, a person rises and labors greatly in Torah. In this way one repairs the fall itself: it becomes an aid to divine service, and one draws service from it. This is in the following month, Kislev, whose letter is samekh and whose attribute is sleep.
records.themeTitle: Rest becomes part of Torah when it restores the capacity to learn
records.themeSummary: The Cheshvan passage explains ‘very good’ sleep by its fruit: rising to renewed effort in Torah.
records.explanation: Cheshvan makes the usefulness of rest explicit: a little sleep enables greater labor afterward, and the apparent descent itself becomes an aid to avodah. This clarifies the present siman’s permission for an interval of diminished consciousness. The continuity lies in the Torah already placed upon the heart and in the renewed life the rest makes possible. It is a purposeful rhythm of service, rather than a demand that one sustain the same intensity at every moment.

records.originHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶהוּ רַק בִּטָּחוֹן, אֲבָל "יִשָּׁעֵן" – מִשְׁעָן הוּא יוֹתֵר, וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּיָדוֹ וְנִשְׁעָן עָלָיו, זֶהוּ "בֵּאלֹהָיו", כִּידוּעַ דְּשֵׁם זֶה מוֹרֶה עַל כֹּחוֹת הַמּוּטְבָּעִים בַּבְּרוּאִים, וֶ"אֱלֹהָיו" רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כֹּחוֹתָיו שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְכַלְכֵּל עַצְמוֹ עַל יָדוֹ בְּכָל צְרָכָיו בְּעֵצוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה וַעֲבוֹדָה – בָּזֶה הוּא עִיקַּר הַשְּׁעִינָה. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יִבְטַח בִּישׁוּעָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִכֹּחוֹ גַּם כֵּן, כִּי אֵין מַעְצוֹר לַה', וְהֵן לֹא קָצְרָה יָדוֹ מֵהוֹשִׁיעַ:
records.originEnglish: Nevertheless, this is trust. “He shall lean” means more: the support that is in his hands, on which he leans, is “on his God.” As is known, this name signifies the powers implanted in created beings. “His God” means the powers he has, which God gave him to sustain himself in all his needs through counsel from Torah, wisdom, and service. This is his principal reliance. Yet he should also trust in deliverance beyond his power, for nothing restrains the Lord, and His hand is not too short to save.
records.targetHebrew: גַּם צָרִיךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בִּתְפִלָּה, לְבַקֵּשׁ עֶזְרָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִן הַיֵּצֶר הַמְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲמִיתוֹ וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ, וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹזֵר לוֹ בְּאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָא. וְזֶה מוֹרֶה אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ: "סוֹמֵךְ הַשֵּׁם לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ; וְכֵן מוֹרֶה אוֹת סָמֶ״ךְ עַל סֻכַּת דָּוִד הַנּוֹפֶלֶת, שֶׁמַּקִּיף כְּסֻכָּה לְהָגֵן עַל מְבַקְשֵׁי עֶזְרָתוֹ לִהְיוֹת סוֹמֵךְ לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים. וּמִצַּד הָאָדָם הָעֵסֶק בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה: לְהַרְגִּיז הַיֵּצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ, עַד שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: At least an awakening from below in prayer is also needed: to ask His help against the inclination that seeks to kill him, which he cannot overcome. God then helps through an awakening from above. Samekh indicates “The Lord supports all who fall,” and the fallen sukkah of David: it surrounds like a sukkah, protecting those who seek His help. From the person’s side, the work of this month is to stir the good inclination against the bad with all his strength, until he cannot overcome it from his own side.
records.themeTitle: Using one’s given powers and praying beyond them belong to the same reliance
records.themeSummary: The work from below uses all available strength and also asks for the help that strength cannot supply by itself.
records.explanation: Kislev joins full effort against the inclination with the prayer that calls forth assistance from above. This explains the present siman’s distinction between leaning on the powers Hashem has already given and trusting in salvation beyond them. Neither side cancels the other: existing wisdom and ability are themselves gifts to be used, while their limitation gives prayer its honest sense of need. Support is received by the person who turns toward Hashem from within that work.

records.originHebrew: וְאַחַר כָּךְ: "וְהָיְתָה יָדְךָ עִמָּדִי" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י) – שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּכַּח וְיִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ, וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי "יָדְךָ", פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּ"יָדְכָה" בְּהֵ"א נִדְרַשׁ יָד כֵּהָה (מְנָחוֹת לז.), אֲבָל "יָדְךָ" הַיְינוּ יָמִין, וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): בִּימִינוֹ זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁיְּמִין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַמַּשְׁפַּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְכַאֲשֶׁר תִּהְיֶה עִמָּדִי אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּשְׁכַּח שֶׁהֲרֵי מַשְׁפַּעַת תָּמִיד. וּלְפִי שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ עַל הַקִּיּוּם, עַל זֶה סָמַךְ תֵּיכֶף בַּקָּשַׁת הַחֲבֵירִים שֶׁהֵם הַמְּקַיְּימִים בְּיָדוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת קפ"ה. וְהִקְדִּים תַּלְמִיד לְחָבֵר, כִּי אָז הָיָה אַחַר פְּטִירַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא, וְנִתְמַנָּה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְפַרְנָס שֶׁעִסְקוֹ הַנְחָלַת הָאָרֶץ וְהִתְחִיל עֵסֶק אַחֵר. רַק יַעְבֵּץ – הוּא עָתְנִיאֵל – לְבָבוֹ הָיָה רוֹעֵשׁ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא דְּהָיָה מְפוּלְפָּל יוֹתֵר מִיהוֹשֻׁעַ, רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ חֲבֵירִים וְלֹא תַלְמִידִים, וּבִקֵּשׁ תְּחִלָּה עַל הַבְּרָכָה בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאַחַר שֶׁהָיָה יְחִידִי בְּלֹא רַב וְחָבֵר וְתַלְמִיד. וְתֵיכֶף לַבְּרָכָה הֻוצְרַךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל הַתַּלְמִידִים שֶׁעַל יָדָם הוּא כְּלִי מַחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְאַחַר הַבְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל הַקִּיּוּם וְשֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח, וְאָז בִּקֵּשׁ עַל הַחֲבֵירִים. וְאַחַר כָּךְ, שֶׁלֹּא יִגְרוֹם אֵיזֶה חֵטְא, בִּקֵּשׁ: "וַעֲשִׂיתָ מֵרָעָה לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי" כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שָׁם, וּמִיָּד: "וַיָּבֵא אֱלֹהִים אֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁאָל]" (שָׁם). וְהִנֵּה בְּרָכָה וְתַלְמִידִים וַחֲבֵירִים אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת מִיָּד כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ; אַךְ הַקִּיּוּם וְשֶׁלֹּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא, לִכְאוֹרָה זֶה אֵין נִתְוַודַּע רַק בְּקֵץ יָמָיו, שֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁנִּתְקַיֵּים בּוֹ כָּל יָמָיו. וְנִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב כַּאֲשֶׁר הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הֵם קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה לֹא יָזוּעַ עוֹד, וְשֶׁאֵין עֲבֵירָה מְכַבַּתּוֹ, כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּי לְפוֹצֵץ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְ"הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט) וּמְסַלֶּקֶת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁמָּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא יִרְאָה גַּבֵּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרָכוֹת ד.). וּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּקִיפוּת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הוּא מְסוּלָּק מִכָּל מִינֵי יְרָאוֹת:
records.originEnglish: Afterward: “May Your hand be with me” (I Chronicles 4:10)—that it should not be forgotten but remain in his possession. This is through “Your hand”: “your hand,” written with the extra letter heh, is interpreted as “the weak hand” (Menachot 37a), but “Your hand” here means the right hand. They said in Berakhot 6a, “At His right hand”—this is Torah, and so forth: God’s right hand imparts words of Torah. When it is with me, forgetting is impossible, for it continually imparts them. Because he asked for permanence, he immediately attached to this the request for companions, who maintain Torah in his possession, as explained above in paragraph 185. He placed the student before the companion because this was after the passing of Moses our teacher; see the Talmud there. Joshua had been appointed leader, occupied with allotting the land, and another occupation had begun. But Jabez—Othniel—had a heart trembling with desire for Torah; see there that he was sharper in reasoning than Joshua. He had neither companions nor students, so he first asked for blessing in Torah, since he was alone without teacher, companion, or student. Immediately with the blessing he had to ask for students, through whom he could become a vessel holding blessing. After the blessing he needed to ask for permanence and that he should not forget; then he asked for companions. Afterward, lest some sin interfere, he asked, “And keep me from evil, that it should not grieve me,” as our Sages explained there. Immediately, “God brought about what he asked.” Blessing, students, and companions could indeed come immediately in the plain sense. But permanence and protection from sin would apparently become known only at life’s end, when he saw that they had endured throughout his life. It seems that even this can be felt in the heart: when the words of Torah are fixed and enduring, he will not move from them, and transgression will not extinguish them, because there is enough in them to shatter the evil inclination. “Wisdom gives strength to the wise” (Ecclesiastes 7:19) and removes the fear that sin might interfere—the fear attributed to Jacob our father (Berakhot 4a). Someone whose strength comes from words of Torah is freed from every kind of fear.
records.targetHebrew: כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּיַעְבֵּץ, אַף שֶׁהָיָה מְנוּגָּב מִכָּל חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהָיָה עוֹסֵק תָּמִיד בַּתּוֹרָה, הִתְפַּלֵּל: "'לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי' – שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׂגִּיבַנִי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּשְׁנוֹת", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּמוּרָה טז עַמּוּד א), שֶׁאַף שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ הָיָה גַּם כֵּן מִתְיָירֵא מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁלֹּא יְבַלְבֵּל דַּעְתּוֹ, וּלְזֶה צָרִיךְ עֶזְרָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.targetEnglish: We find this with Jabez: although he was emptied of all this world’s desires and constantly engaged in Torah, he prayed, “‘That it should not grieve me’—that the evil inclination should not overpower me and prevent my study,” as stated in Temurah 16a. Even while sitting in the study hall he feared that the evil inclination would confuse his mind. For this he needs help from the blessed God.
records.themeTitle: Even established learning needs prayer that it will continue to bear fruit
records.themeSummary: Yaavetz asks for protection from interruption while already immersed in Torah, not only before beginning to learn.
records.explanation: Lech Lecha emphasizes that Yaavetz’s existing devotion did not make him independent of divine assistance. This helps explain why the present siman distinguishes a blessing in Torah from the further requests for retention, companions, and protection from sin. Receiving an insight and becoming a vessel in which it can endure are different needs. The prayer concerns the continuing life of Torah within the learner, including the ability to remain available for study and teaching.

records.originEnglish: As I heard, the four cubits of halakhah are holy with the holiness of the Land of Israel. The air of foreign lands is entirely expelled from them on every side by the two-edged sword, and the holy air of words of Torah enters. This is the air of the Land of Israel, which therefore makes one wise, corresponding to Torah’s quality of making the simple wise.
records.targetHebrew: וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים דְּמִשְׁתַּדְּלֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא אִתְקְרִיאוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג כט ב וְשָׁם קכד סוֹף עַמּוּד ב), שֶׁהֵם יְכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה תָּמִיד מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא כַּשַּׁבָּתוֹת, וּלְעוֹלָם יִרְשׁוּ אָרֶץ, שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לֶאֱכוֹל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִקְּדוּשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְזֶהוּ שַׁיָּיכוּת בְּרִית וְתוֹרָה לְבִרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ.
records.targetEnglish: Torah scholars who labor in Torah are called Shabbatot, as stated in Zohar III, 29b and 124b. Through Torah’s power they can continually attain a foretaste of the World to Come, like Shabbatot, and “they shall inherit the Land forever”: they merit eating in this world from the Land of Israel’s holiness. This is the connection of covenant and Torah to the blessing for the Land.
records.themeTitle: Torah makes a foretaste of sacred place available within present life
records.themeSummary: Tu BiShvat develops the connection between Torah, a foretaste of the World to Come, and the holiness of Eretz Yisrael.
records.explanation: Tu BiShvat explains how the power of Torah allows a talmid chacham to receive a foretaste associated with Shabbat and the Land even within this world. This develops the present siman’s description of the four amos of halakhah as a place whose atmosphere is changed by Torah. The claim concerns an enacted holiness of learning, not simply a geographical comparison: the person enters the air of Torah by turning toward its words.

records.originHebrew: וְכָל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לוֹמַר פָּרָשָׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁתְּחִלַּת קַבָּלָתוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּעִנְיָן זֶה, גַּם לִהְיוֹת מוּפְקָר אִם יִהְיֶה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּךְ. רַק מִי שֶׁמַּנְהִיג בְּמִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וְהַגְדָּרָה, הוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ וְכוּלֵי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָן, שֶׁאֵין זֶה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְכֵן אֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם הַיְחִידִים צְרִיכִים גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְרַשְׁבִּ"י בְּשַׁבָּת (לג:) שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר לַמְּעָרָה, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת כֵּן רַק בַּמְּעָרָה וְחוּץ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה בְּיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם, וְ"לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מה, יח). וְהַנְהָגָה זוֹ לָצֵאת מִגְּבוּלוֹ וּמִכְּפִי שֶׁהוּא כְּלִי לְקַבֵּל בְּעוֹדוֹ בַּגּוּף – זֶהוּ הַנְהָגָה מֵעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ כַּנּוֹדָע סוֹדָם, שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ לְקַבֵּל שֶׁפַע אוֹר שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִכֹּחַ הַמַּגְבִּילָם הַמְּכוּנֶּה בְּשֵׁם כְּלִי. רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא בִּכְלִי הַגּוּף הַמַּגְדִּיר, אָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית כב:): נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתִּי בְּךָ הַחֲיֶיהָ, וְלֹא יַפְקִיר לְגַמְרֵי לָצֵאת מִגְּבוּל כְּלִי הַגּוּף; רַק צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בּוֹ כֹּחַ זוֹ שֶׁל הַהֶפְקֵר לְגַמְרֵי גַּם כֵּן; רַק אֵצֶל הַיָּחִיד זֶה בְּתֹקֶף וְלָרַבִּים זֶה, אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ לִשְׁנֵיהֶם.
records.originEnglish: Everyone must also recite the first paragraph [of the Shema]: at the beginning of his daily acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven, he must be disposed in this way, even to surrender everything if this should be God’s will. A person who conducts himself according to the ordinary way of the world and within bounds does so because “many acted … and did not succeed”: this is not God’s will [for them]. Even those exceptional individuals must also recite “If you indeed listen,” just as Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai was told to return to the cave. For this is possible only in a cave, outside this world; within this world, the Holy One desires its habitation—“He did not create it for desolation.” A way of acting that goes beyond one’s bounds and beyond what one is a vessel to receive while in the body belongs to the world of chaos: they sought to receive an abundance of light beyond the limiting power called a vessel. But in this world, within the body’s limiting vessel, the Sages said, “Sustain the soul I have given you.” One must not surrender everything so as to leave the bounds of the bodily vessel. Yet the power of complete surrender must also be present. In the exceptional individual this [power] is stronger, and among the many the other [mode] is stronger; nevertheless, everyone needs both.
records.targetHebrew: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד בְּנִסָּיוֹן זֶה, הָא רָבָא בְּעַצְמוֹ אָמַר (בְּרָכוֹת שָׁם): "בְּיוֹמֵי נִיסָן וּבְיוֹמֵי תִּשְׁרֵי לָא תִּתְחֲזוּ קַמַּאי וְכוּלֵי", הֲרֵי שֶׁאַף שֶׁהָיוּ אָמוֹרָאִים וְרַבָּנָן תַּלְמִידָיו, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁהֶעְדֵּר הַמְּזוֹנוֹת יַטְרִיד לָהֶם, צִוָּה שֶׁיַּעַסְקוּ בְּפַרְנָסָתָם בִּימֵי נִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי. וְעַל זֶה מַיְירֵי הַפָּרָשָׁה: "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺתַי וְגוֹמֵר וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר", דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מִצְוֹת ה' שֶׁצִּוָּה לִשְׁבּוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת וּשְׁמִיטָה, אֲבָל אֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם לִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי רַק לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה, וְזֶהוּ "מְלַאכְתָּן נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי עַצְמָן". אֲבָל מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת דְּרוֹפְתְּקֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא לִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי רַק לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה כִּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, מְלַאכְתּוֹ נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים, וְלָאו כָּל אָדָם זוֹכֶה לָזֶה. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ וְכוּלֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָן".
records.targetEnglish: But for someone unable to withstand this trial, Rava himself said, “In the days of Nisan and the days of Tishrei, do not appear before me ….” Although they were amoraim and sages, his students, since he knew that a lack of food would distract them, he instructed them to attend to their livelihood in Nisan and Tishrei. This is the subject of the passage, “If you indeed listen to My commandments … you shall gather your grain …”: they perform God’s commandments, resting on Shabbat and in the sabbatical year as He commanded. But they do not perform the Omnipresent’s will of being free solely for the toil of Torah. This is “their work is performed by themselves.” One who merits to be a vessel for Torah’s toil, free solely for it according to the Omnipresent’s will, has his work performed by others. Not everyone merits this. Thus the Talmud says: “Many acted … according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and did not succeed.”
records.themeTitle: Rava’s instruction to earn a livelihood makes the limits of imitation concrete
records.themeSummary: Even accomplished talmidim were told to provide for their needs when lack of sustenance would disrupt their Torah.
records.explanation: Lech Lecha gives a practical case of the present siman’s distinction between total willingness to surrender and the form of service suited to one’s actual vessel. Rava directed his talmidim to work in the relevant seasons because he knew that deprivation would disturb their learning. This is why reciting both paragraphs of Shema matters: unreserved allegiance to Hashem must also be carried into the sustaining conduct that permits Torah and mitzvot to endure in embodied life.

records.originHebrew: דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁעוֹבְרִים דֶּרֶךְ הַלֵּב – פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהַלֵּב מַרְגִּישׁ וּמִתְפַּעֵל בָּהֶם – הוּא נִקְרָא "עֵץ חַיִּים" וְסַמָּא דְּחַיֵּי. כִּי הַלֵּב מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כג), וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְפַּעֵל, הֲרֵי שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתוֹ מִתְפַּעֵל עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמוֹלִידָה חַיּוּת בָּאָדָם. וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ, כִּי הַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן", וְיִרְאָה נוּקְבָא וְתוֹרַת אֱמֶת דְּכַר לְהַשְׁלִים וּלְשַׂמֵּחַ הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פִּקּוּדֵי ה' יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב]" (תְּהִלִּים יט, ט), אַחַר הַיִּרְאָה הַמּוֹלֶדֶת לֵב נִשְׁבָּר וְעַצְבוּת.
records.originEnglish: Words of Torah that pass through the heart—that is, the heart feels them and is affected by them—are called “a tree of life” and a medicine of life. The heart is the source of vitality, as it says, “From it are the outgoings of life”; when it is affected, the very root of the person’s life is affected by the words of Torah, and they generate life within him. This happens when his fear of sin precedes his wisdom. Fear is in the heart, as the sages explain concerning “but there is no heart.” Fear is the feminine aspect, while the Torah of truth is the masculine aspect, completing and gladdening the heart, as it says, “The precepts of the Lord are upright, gladdening the heart,” after the fear that produces a broken heart and sadness.
records.targetHebrew: וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לַמְיַחֲלִים לְחַסְדּוֹ", לִהְיוֹת הַתִּקּוּן עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִיא תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד עַל לְשׁוֹנָהּ. וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּעַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בִּפְרָט אָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳): שֶׁאֵין מִתְקַיֵּם אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁדַּעְתוֹ שְׁפָלָה, שֶׁתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִמְשַׁל לְמַשְׁקִין, "יֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְּתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה" (וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר י״ד), וְהִיא מִתְקַיֵּם רַק בְּמִי שֶׁדַּעְתוֹ שְׁפָלָה וְנִשְׁבַּר לִבּוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: Of this it says, “Those who hope for His kindness”: the repair comes through Oral Torah, which is “the Torah of kindness upon her tongue.” We have already said that specifically concerning Oral Torah they taught that it endures only in one whose mind is humble. Oral Torah is compared to liquids—the “wine of Oral Torah,” as explained in the fourteenth discourse—and it endures only in one whose mind is humble and whose heart is broken within him.
records.themeTitle: Humility lets Oral Torah enter as nourishment rather than remain external knowledge
records.themeSummary: Torah compared to liquid is received in a lowered, receptive mind and a heart that recognizes its need.
records.explanation: Chanukah applies the image of liquid to Oral Torah and makes humility the condition for its endurance. This clarifies the present siman’s contrast between understanding an idea intellectually and having Torah pass through the heart. The broken heart is a receptive vessel, not the goal in isolation: it permits the Torah received there to become life, healing, and joy. That is why awe before wisdom can lead to a deeper and more lasting love of Torah.

records.originHebrew: כָּל הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת וּשְׂרָרָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלֹכוּ" (מִשְׁלֵי ח, טו). וְלָכֵן סָמוּךְ לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה וּבְאוֹתָהּ פָּרָשָׁה נֶאֱמַר הִתְמַנּוּת הָרָאשִׁים. וְהָיָה זֶה עַל יְדֵי יִתְרוֹ, דְּבֶאֱמֶת נֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית אֵין יָכוֹל לִסְבּוֹל הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל, אֲפִילּוּ מִן הַגָּדוֹל בְּחָכְמָה, לְפִי שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב" (דְּבָרִים לג, ד), כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הַהוּא עַם הָאָרֶץ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשַׁת צַו פָּרָשָׁה ט), וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּכָל אֶחָד אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּאוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה, וְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁחָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת פָּסוּל, וְאִם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁזֶּה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ זֶה לָזֶה. וְהֲגַם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל זֶה הַקָּטָן כְּלוּם. וְזֶה טַעַם (תַּעֲנִית ז.): "וּמִתַּלְמִידַי יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם", כִּי רַב אֵין לָאָדָם רַק אֶחָד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.): כָּל הַלּוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה מֵרַב אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי, גְּמָרָא מֵרַב אֶחָד עָדִיף; וַאֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ יוֹתֵר, מִכָּל מָקוֹם חֲבֵירִים מְרוּבִּים יוֹתֵר כַּנּוֹדָע, וְתַלְמִידִים יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם דִּלְזֶה אֵין קֵץ, וְהוּא קוֹלֵט כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁבְּכָל אֶחָד שֶׁאֵין נִמְצָא בּוֹ, וְנִמְצָא לָמַד מֵהֶם יוֹתֵר לְרִבּוּיָם.
records.originEnglish: All elevation and authority come through words of Torah, as it is written, “Through me kings reign” (Proverbs 8:15). Therefore the appointment of leaders is stated close to the giving of the Torah, in the same portion. This came about through Yitro, for in truth the soul of Israel cannot tolerate superiority at all, even from someone greater in wisdom, because all Israel have a share in the Torah, as it is written, “An inheritance of the congregation of Jacob” (Deuteronomy 33:4). This is what that unlearned man said to Rabbi Yannai in the Midrash Rabbah, Tzav, chapter 9. As is known, each person has a hold in a letter of the Torah, and a Torah scroll missing a single letter is invalid. Thus, just as this person needs that one, that one needs this person. Although one has a larger share in words of Torah, he nevertheless knows nothing of the portion belonging to this lesser person. This explains “From my students, more than from them all” (Taanit 7a). A person has only one teacher, as it says (Avodah Zarah 19a), “Whoever studies Torah from one teacher,” and so forth: for received teaching, one teacher is preferable. Even if he has more, his companions are more numerous, as is known, and his students are the most numerous of all, for there is no limit to this. He absorbs the words of Torah that are in each of them and are absent from him, and consequently learns more from them because of their number.
records.targetHebrew: וְחָלַם לִי דְּהַפֵּרוּשׁ הַפָּשׁוּט: דְּיֵשׁ פְּעָמִים מְרִיבָה כְּעִנְיַן (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כ״א עַמּוּד א׳) "קִנְאַת סוֹפְרִים תַּרְבֶּה חָכְמָה", וּמַחֲלֹקֶת לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁהִיא לְטוֹבָה וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּצְמַח מִמֶּנָּה דְּבָרִים טוֹבִים [אַךְ בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל׳ אִיתָא: "אֵין דָּבָר טוֹב וְאֵין שָׁלוֹם יוֹצֵא מִתּוֹךְ מְרִיבָה", עַד כָּאן]; אֲבָל זֶה הַטּוֹב שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם [שֶׁהוּא חִבּוּר הַשְּׁלֵמוּת וּכְלִי הַמַּחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְיָחִיד לִהְיוֹת שָׁלֵם בַּכֹּל, רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהֵם בְּאַחְדוּת אָז יֵשׁ חִבּוּר כָּל הַשְּׁלֵמוּת, וְשָׁלוֹם שָׁרְשׁוֹ "שָׁלֵם", וְתוֹסֶפֶת וָא"ו מוֹרָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם עַל הַחִבּוּר] אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמְּרִיבָה, אַף שֶׁהִיא טוֹבָה וּלְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
records.targetEnglish: I dreamt that the plain meaning was this: sometimes there is contention of the kind described as “The rivalry of scholars increases wisdom” (Bava Batra 21a), and a dispute for the sake of Heaven that is beneficial and from which good things may grow [although Shemot Rabbah, chapter 30, says: “No good thing and no peace emerge from contention”; end of quotation]. But this particular good of peace [which is the joining of completeness and the vessel that holds blessing: an individual cannot be complete in everything; only through their unity is there a joining of all completeness. Shalom, “peace,” has the root shalem, “complete,” and the added letter vav indicates connection everywhere] cannot emerge from contention, even when it is good and for the sake of Heaven.
records.themeTitle: Peace joins portions of Torah that no single learner possesses alone
records.themeSummary: The good of peace is a joined completeness, distinct from the increased wisdom that a productive dispute may generate.
records.explanation: Divrei Chalomot distinguishes the good gained through rivalry in learning from the particular good called peace. Peace joins contributions that are individually incomplete. This illuminates the present siman’s insistence that even a great scholar lacks the smallest person’s unique portion of Torah. The need for teachers and functional authority in this world remains, but it gives no ground for contempt: no size of one person’s portion makes another’s portion dispensable.

records.originHebrew: וְעִיקַּר סְמִיכַת נוֹפְלִים מִמַּדְרֵגָתָן הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנּוֹתֶנֶת עֹז וְתוּשִׁיָּה. וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר שֶׁל אֱמֶת בְּהַכָּרַת מַעֲלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הֲגַם שֶׁהוּא מְרוּחָק מִמֶּנּוּ בְּתַכְלִית, שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, וְזֶה אֶפְשָׁר גַּם בְּעֵת הַנְּפִילָה וְהָרִחוּק, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִסְמָךְ. אֲבָל תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהוּא כְּעוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ, הַיְינוּ מְקוֹרָב, זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּעֵת נְפִילָה שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ מְקוֹרָב; וְגַם אִי אֶפְשָׁר בִּתְפִלָּה לֶעָנִי מִפְּאַת שִׁבְרוּת לֵב, שֶׁגַּם לָזֶה צָרִיךְ חִזּוּק, וּבְעֵת נְפִילָה אַף זֶה אֵין לוֹ, רַק הַלֵּב מְטוּמְטָם כְּאֶבֶן לְגַמְרֵי. וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב:): מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, אִם אֶבֶן וְכוּלֵי הוּא מִתְפּוֹצֵץ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא נִסְמָךְ וְנִתְחַזֵּק לְהִתְעוֹרֵר לָקוּם מִנְּפִילָתוֹ.
records.originEnglish: The principal support of those who fall from their level comes through words of Torah, which give strength and sound counsel. This comes through truthful speech recognizing the greatness of the blessed God, even when the person is utterly distant from Him. Such is Torah: one is not standing before the King, so this is possible even during the fall and distance, and through it one is supported. Prayer, however, is like standing before the King, being close to Him; this is not possible at the time of the fall, since the person is not close. Even the prayer of the poor person from a broken heart is then impossible, for that too requires strength, and at the time of the fall the person lacks even this: the heart is completely blocked, like a stone. Concerning this they said, ‘Draw him to the study house; if he is stone … he shatters.’ Through words of Torah the person is supported and strengthened to awaken and rise from the fall.
records.targetHebrew: וְאָמַר שָׁם: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן סְמָכָן דָּוִד בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "סוֹמֵךְ הַשֵּׁם לְכָל הַנֹּפְלִים"; וּכְתִיב: "סֻכַּת דָּוִיד הַנֹּפֶלֶת", כִּי סֻכָּה דִּירַת עֲרַאי, וְהַיְינוּ אַף בְּעֵת שֶׁנִּרְאֵית כְּנוֹפֶלֶת הוּא סְמָכָהּ, שֶׁמַּמְשִׁיךְ מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם תָּמִיד. וְהַנְּפִילָה הוּא צֹרֶךְ עֲלִיָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם", וְלֶעָתִיד כְּתִיב: "אָקִים אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִיד הַנֹּפֶלֶת".
records.targetEnglish: The Gemara says there: nevertheless, David supported them through the holy spirit, as it says, ‘The Lord supports all who fall.’ It is also written, ‘the fallen sukkah of David,’ for a sukkah is a temporary dwelling. Thus, even when it appears fallen, he supports it, continually drawing the attribute of His blessed kingship into the world. The fall is for the sake of ascent, as it says, ‘A righteous person falls seven times and rises.’ Concerning the future it is written, ‘I will raise up the fallen sukkah of David.’
records.themeTitle: Divine support can be present while a person still feels fallen
records.themeSummary: The fallen sukkah of David represents kingship sustained within the very condition that appears to contradict it.
records.explanation: Cheshvan explains that the sukkah is supported even while it appears fallen, and that the fall can become the setting of ascent. This gives the present siman’s opening confidence a concrete image. The person need not first recover a full feeling of closeness before speaking truth about Hashem or turning to Torah. Those words are themselves a means of support through which the capacity to rise and pray can return.

records.originHebrew: הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין לַיֵּצֶר כִּמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁאֵין לִבּוֹ נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי בַּהֲרִיגַת הַיֵּצֶר מִכֹּל וָכֹל, אִם הוּא מְמוּלָּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כָּל צָרְכּוֹ, הֲרֵי הַיֵּצֶר מִתַּבֵּל לִהְיוֹת דָּבָר הָרָאוּי.
records.originEnglish: Torah is a seasoning for the inclination, as our sages said. Even someone whose heart is not entirely pure, who has not completely slain the inclination, can have the inclination seasoned into something fit, if he is filled with words of Torah to the extent he needs.
records.targetHebrew: וְאָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה הָעֵצָה: "הַאֲכִילֵהוּ לָחֶם" וְלֹא יַזִּיק לְךָ, כִּי כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם רוֹצֶה בַּתּוֹרָה לְהִנָּצֵל מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע, אָז תּוֹעִיל הַתּוֹרָה לְטוֹבָה, "כִּי גֶחָלִים אַתָּה חֹתֶה עַל רֹאשׁוֹ", וְלֹא תִּתֵּן הַתּוֹרָה כֹּחַ בַּקְּלִפָּה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
records.targetEnglish: Solomon said that in Torah the counsel is: “Feed him bread,” and it will not harm you. When a person desires Torah in order to escape the evil inclination, the Torah will help for the good: “You are heaping coals upon his head.” The Torah will not give strength to the husk, God forbid.
records.themeTitle: A sincere turn to Torah can begin before the heart is fully purified
records.themeSummary: Kislev explains why Torah does not simply strengthen the remaining mixture when the learner seeks it as a remedy for the inclination.
records.explanation: The Kislev passage answers the difficulty implicit in the opening of this siman: how can Torah help someone whose heart is not yet clean? Its stated direction matters—the person wants Torah in order to escape the inclination. Torah then acts as the seasoning Rav Tzadok describes, making the existing power fit for good. Perfect purity is not a prerequisite for beginning this work; seeking Torah’s correction is part of the work itself.

records.originHebrew: וְעַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר, כִּי יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁקָע וְלִהְיוֹת "מָצָא מִין אֶת מִינוֹ וְנִיעוֹר". אֲבָל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְנוּקֶּה בְּחַדְרֵי לִבּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר יֵשׁ לוֹ יִתְרוֹן עַל הַבְּהֵמָה מִצַּד חָכְמָתוֹ. וְלָכֵן עַל יְדֵי מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא מוֹצִיא כֹּחַ אוֹתָהּ נֶפֶשׁ מֵהִתְלַבְּשׁוּתָהּ בְּנֶפֶשׁ בַּהֲמִית וְכֹחַ בְּהֵמָה. וְכֵן בַּפּוֹעַל, הֲרֵי מִתְהַפֵּךְ בְּשַׂר הַבְּהֵמָה לְהָזִין גּוּפוֹ וְלִהְיוֹת נַעֲשָׂה בְּשַׂר אָדָם, כָּךְ בַּכֹּחַ מִתְהַפֵּךְ כֹּחַ בַּהֲמִי לְכֹחַ אָדָם. וְזֶה טַעַם מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר: "בְּחָכְמָה אִתְבְּרִירוּ", וְהַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם יָכוֹל לְבָרֵר וּלְתַקֵּן נְפָשׁוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא אֵין מְנוּקֶּה לְגַמְרֵי מֵאוֹתָן דְּבָרִים; רַק אִם נַפְשׁוֹ מְשׁוּקַּעַת בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא מַעֲלֶה וּמְתַקֵּן כָּל מִינֵי מַחְשְׁבוֹת זָרוֹת.
records.originEnglish: An unlearned person is forbidden, for he may become submerged, so that “one kind finds its own kind and is awakened.” But a Torah scholar, even if he is not cleansed in the chambers of his heart, nevertheless already has an advantage over the animal through his wisdom. Through his thought in words of Torah he therefore brings the power of that soul out of its clothing in an animal soul and animal power. Just as, in actuality, the animal’s flesh is transformed to nourish his body and become human flesh, so, in its power, animal power is transformed into human power. This is the reason for the Zohar’s statement, “They are clarified through wisdom.” A Torah scholar can clarify and repair souls even though he is not wholly cleansed of those things himself. Provided that his soul is immersed in words of Torah, through those words he raises and repairs all kinds of foreign thoughts.
records.targetHebrew: אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת, גַּם בְּבָשָׂר מָצִינוּ (פְּסָחִים קט עַמּוּד א): "אֵין שִׂמְחָה אֶלָּא בְּבָשָׂר", וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזּוֹכִין לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּלִישְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה"; וְאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל נִצְרַךְ הַבָּשָׂר, שֶׁבְּבָשָׂר יֵשׁ יוֹתֵר נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים לְהוֹצִיא מִמַּה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לְהוֹצִיא מִן הַצְּמָחִים; וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ֣י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קמ עַמּוּד ב): דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: "וְלָא בַּעֲתִירוּתַי אֲכַלִי יַרְקָא וְכוּלֵי, דַּאֲמִינָא: הֵיכָא דְּעָיֵיל יַרְקָא לֵיעוּל בִּשְׂרָא וְכַוְורֵי", שֶׁאֵין הַמְּכֻוָּון חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁלְּהִתְעַנֵּג בָּחַר בְּבָשָׂר וְדָגִים, רַק פֵּירוּשׁ "בַּעֲתִירוּתַי" – הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְהוּתַּר לוֹ הַבָּשָׂר, דְּעַם הָאָרֶץ אָסוּר לֶאֱכֹל בָּשָׂר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים מט עַמּוּד ב); וְאָז לֹא אָכַל יַרְקָא מֵאֲשֶׁר יֵשׁ יוֹתֵר לְהוֹצִיא נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים מִבַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים מִמַּה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לְהוֹצִיא מִן הַצְּמָחִים, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אָמַר: "הֵיכָא דְּעָיֵיל יַרְקָא לֵיעוּל בִּשְׂרָא וְכַוְורֵי", עַד כָּאן. וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת מד עַמּוּד ב): "כָּל נֶפֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְכָל הַקָּרוֹב לַנֶּפֶשׁ מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְכוּלֵי", וְהַמְּכֻוָּון גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים יוֹתֵר.
records.targetEnglish: In truth, concerning meat too we find: “There is no joy except with meat.” This means meriting straightness of heart, as it is said, “Joy for the upright of heart.” After the damage, meat is needed because there are more holy sparks to bring out from meat than from plants. Thus the Ari explains Rav Chisda’s statement in Shabbat: “In my wealth I did not eat vegetables, for I said: where vegetables would enter, let meat and fish enter.” God forbid that his meaning was to choose meat and fish for pleasure. Rather, “in my wealth” means when he became a Torah scholar and meat was permitted to him, since an unlearned person is forbidden to eat meat, as stated in Pesachim. He then did not eat vegetables because there are more holy sparks to bring out from animals than from plants; therefore he said, “Where vegetables would enter, let meat and fish enter.” This is the end of that explanation. This is also the meaning of their saying in Berakhot: “Every living thing restores the soul, and whatever is near the soul restores the soul”: it too means that there are more holy sparks in it.
records.themeTitle: Elevating a bodily power requires a purpose beyond its enjoyment
records.themeSummary: Rav Chisda’s eating is interpreted through the Torah work made possible by the food’s vitality, rather than through luxury.
records.explanation: Lech Lecha applies the same account of holy sparks to a particular sage’s conduct and expressly rejects pleasure as its intended explanation. This helps make the present siman’s transformation of animal vitality into human vitality intelligible. The physical nourishment is real, but its spiritual elevation depends on the Torah that directs the life it sustains. Merely choosing a richer food does not by itself establish the clarification described here.

records.originHebrew: וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אַדְּרַבָּה יָשַׁן הַרְבֵּה, וְעָלָיו נֶאֱמַר: "כֵּן יִתֵּן לִידִידוֹ שֵׁנָא" (תְּהִלִּים קכז, ב), וְכִמְאַמַּר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יב) שֶׁיָּשַׁן עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת וּמַפְתְּחוֹת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְכוּלֵי; כִּי הוּא כְּמוֹ אִסְטְמָא לְפַרְזְלָא. דְּמִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּרְזֶל כַּנּוֹדָע, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וָאֵרָא (כד ב) שֶׁהוּא מֵעָפָר וּבוֹ תּוֹקֶף הַבֵּירוּרִים מִפְּסֹלֶת הֶעָפָר עַל יְדֵי הַהַכְנָסָה בָּאֵשׁ דְּאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה] עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אִסְטְמָא, וְהוּא מִדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.  וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (סב:): "שֵׁינָה בְּעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כְּאִסְטְמָא לְפַרְזְלָא". וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּעִיקָּר כְּאוֹתוֹ הַפֵּירוּשׁ דְּרַשִּׁ"י שֶׁהוּא טוֹב, כִּי בְּעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר הוּא יִחוּד חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה, דְּהַיְינוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ כַּנּוֹדָע; וְאָז גְּמַר שֵׁינַת הַלַּיְלָה שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְאוֹתָהּ רֶגַע הוּא מִדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְאָז הַשֵּׁינָה טוֹבָה כְּאִסְטְמָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְכֵן אָמְרוּ (שָׁם נה סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) כִּי הַחֲלוֹמוֹת שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לְעַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר מִתְקַיְּימִים, כִּי הֵם מִכְּלַל אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים בִּנְבוּאָה, שֶׁכְּבָר כָּלוּ דִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְהִרְהוּרֵי דְּיוֹמָא, וְזֶה מִצַּד הַשֵּׁינָה הַטּוֹבָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
records.originEnglish: King Solomon, on the contrary, slept much. Of him it is said, “Thus He gives sleep to His beloved”; our sages relate that he slept until four hours into the day, with the keys of the Temple. For he is like the finishing treatment of iron. King David’s quality is iron, as is known, and the Zohar explains that he is of earth. In him is the force of clarifying the waste from the earth through entering the fire of love and awe, until it receives its finishing treatment: this is the quality of King Solomon. The sages said, “Sleep at dawn is like the finishing treatment of iron.” I heard that the principal meaning is the interpretation of Rashi that takes this positively. At dawn is the union of the sun and moon, the union of the Holy One and His Presence. Then the night’s sleep, the quality of David, reaches completion; that moment belongs to Solomon’s quality. Then sleep is beneficial, like that finishing treatment. They likewise said that dreams close to dawn are fulfilled, for these belong to one-sixtieth of prophecy: the day’s imaginings and thoughts have already come to an end. This proceeds from good sleep.
records.targetHebrew: וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לְכָל חָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה, חָכְמָה תַּתָּאָה, עַל יְדֵי חֲלוֹם אֶחָד, וּכְתִיב: "וַיֶּחְכַּם מִכָּל הָאָדָם וְגוֹמֵר", וְאֵין אֹפֶן לְהַשִּׂיג חָכְמָה זוֹ בְּהָקִיץ; וְשֵׁינָה זוֹ טוֹב מְאֹד, וְהִיא תַּרְדֵּמַת נְבוּאָה שֶׁמַּשִּׂיג הַרְבֵּה בַּתּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה עוֹמֵד וְיָגֵעַ בַּתּוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה.
records.targetEnglish: King Solomon attained all the wisdom of Solomon, lower wisdom, through one dream. “He was wiser than all men.” There is no way to attain this wisdom while awake. Such sleep is very good: it is the deep sleep of prophecy, in which he attains much in Torah and thereby rises and labors greatly in Torah.
records.themeTitle: Shlomo’s sleep represents receiving wisdom after the stage of struggle
records.themeSummary: His dream illustrates why rest can belong to an attainment of Torah, rather than only to an interruption of it.
records.explanation: Kislev identifies Shlomo’s dream as the setting in which his distinctive wisdom was received, and relates that sleep to renewed labor in Torah. This develops the present siman’s contrast between David’s struggle and Shlomo’s settled stage. The sleep is valuable through what it receives and what it enables afterward. The example therefore explains a particular completed stage; it does not make every sleep equivalent to Shlomo’s prophetic reception.

records.originHebrew: עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁינָה הָרְאוּיָה בְּלֹא חֲלוֹמוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים וְזָרִים, הוּא יָכוֹל בְּקַל בַּהַשְׁכָּמָה לִמְצוֹא יִחוּל לְבָבוֹ לְיִרְאַת ה'. וּלְכָךְ מְסַיֶּימֶת בִּרְכַּת הַמַּפִּיל, שֶׁהוּא בַּקָּשָׁה לְהִנָּצֵל מֵחֲלוֹמוֹת רָעִים וְהִרְהוּרִים רָעִים, מִטַּעַם: כִּי "אַתָּה הַמַּפִּיל וְגוֹמֵר" וּמִמְּךָ הוּא הַשֵּׁינָה וְאֵין לְךָ לִגְרוֹם לִי רַע. וּמְסַיֵּים: "הַמֵּאִיר לָעוֹלָם וְגוֹמֵר", דְּאוֹר הַשַּׁחַר שֶׁמֵּאִיר לָעוֹלָם יִהְיֶה בִּכְבוֹדוֹ, בְּהַכָּרַת כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם, כְּטַעַם "כָּל פָּעַל לַמַּעֲנֵהוּ" – לְקִילּוּסוֹ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים מִזְמוֹר קמח).
records.originEnglish: Through proper sleep, without bad, alien dreams and thoughts, a person can readily find upon rising that the heart longs for awe of God. The blessing Hamapil, which asks to be saved from bad dreams and harmful thoughts, therefore concludes on the ground that “You are the One who casts sleep…”: sleep comes from You, and You should not cause me harm. It ends, “Who illuminates the world…”: the dawn’s light that illuminates the world should be “with His glory,” through recognition of Heaven’s glory, in the sense of “Everything He has made is for His purpose”—for His praise.
records.targetHebrew: וְכֵן תִּקְּנוּ בַּבְּרָכָה עַל הַשֵּׁינָה שֶׁמַּתְחֶלֶת: "הַמַּפִּיל חֶבְלֵי שֵׁינָה עַל עֵינָי וְכוּלֵיהּ", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁמַּפִּיל חֶבְלֵי שֵׁינָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה כְּלָל, וּמְסַיֵּם: "הַמֵּאִיר לָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בִּכְבוֹדוֹ", שֶׁאַדְּרַבָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לָאָדָם עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁינָה, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהוּא סוֹבֵב בְּאוֹר מַקִּיף וְשׁוֹמֵר, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלֶךָ וְשָׁמַר רַגְלְךָ [מִלָּכֶד]";
records.targetEnglish: They therefore established the blessing over sleep to begin, “Who casts the bonds of sleep upon my eyes…”—He casts sleep so that one cannot see at all—and to conclude, “Who illuminates the entire world with His glory.” On the contrary, God illuminates a person through sleep, by surrounding one with an encompassing light and guarding one, as it is said, “For the Lord will be your confidence, and will guard your foot [from being caught].”
records.themeTitle: HaMapil joins the closing of the eyes to a request for illumination
records.themeSummary: The beginning and end of the blessing describe sleep as dependence on Hashem’s guarding light.
records.explanation: Kislev comments on the same transition in HaMapil that this siman explains: the eyes cease seeing, yet the blessing concludes with illumination. This clarifies why the siman prays for sleep that will make the morning’s recognition of Heaven easier. The desired light is not ordinary sight continuing uninterrupted through the night; it is the guarding and inward renewal received while conscious control is set aside.

records.originHebrew: וְזֶה טַעַם שֶׁקִּבֵּל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מַתָּנוֹת מִמִּצְרַיִם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִשְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וְהָיוּ מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ חָכְמָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא), שֶׁקָּלַט הַחֵשֶׁק לְחָכְמָה שֶׁלָּהֶם, רַק שֶׁהוּא חָשַׁק לְחָכְמַת אֱמֶת. וְכָךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קִבֵּל רוּחַ חָכְמָה וּבִינָה מִמִּצְרַיִם, וְרוּחַ עֵצָה וּגְבוּרָה מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ; וְשֶׁזֶּה טַעַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ: מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ נִתְעַבְּרָה שָׂרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת), כִּי בְּעֵת שֶׁנִּיטַּל כֹּחַ הַהוֹלָדָה מֵאֲבִימֶלֶךְ, אָז נִיתַּן כֹּחוֹ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.  וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַבְטָחַת: "יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל" (בְּרֵאשִׁית טו, יד) וּבִזַּת הַיָּם, וְהוּא הֲכָנָה לְחָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה. רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם שָׁרְשׁוֹ מִצַּד חָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת; וּבִשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נֶאֱמַר: "וַתֵּרֶב חָכְמַת וְגוֹמֵר וּמִכָּל חָכְמַת מִצְרָיִם" (מְלָכִים א ה, י), דְּהַיְינוּ בְּחָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם. וְכָל חֵשֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹה הָיָה לְחָכְמָה, שֶׁעַל זֶה בִּיקֵּשׁ בַּחֲלוֹם רַק זֶה. וְכָךְ כֹּחוֹ קָבוּעַ בָּרְכוּשׁ, וּלְזֶה חָשַׁק שִׁישַׁק, וְחָזַר לִמְקוֹמוֹ; כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת חָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת הוּא חֶלְקָם, רַק שֶׁהָיָה בִּשְׁאֵלָה לְשָׁעָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְצוֹרֶךְ לִקְבּוֹעַ בְּלִבָּם עַל יְדֵי זֶה חָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְעַד שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁחִבֵּר מִשְׁלֵי בְּבֵירוּר חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה, וְאָז לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ עוֹד לְחָכְמַת חִיצוֹנוֹת, וְחָזַר כָּל אֶחָד לִמְקוֹמוֹ.
records.originEnglish: This is why Abraham our father accepted gifts from Egypt. Through them he merited that his two kidneys were like two teachers, teaching him wisdom, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah: he absorbed their desire for wisdom, but his desire was for true wisdom. I similarly heard that Abraham our father received a spirit of wisdom and understanding from Egypt, and a spirit of counsel and might from Abimelech. This explains [the scoffers’] claim that Sarah became pregnant from Abimelech: when the power of procreation was taken from Abimelech, his power was given to Abraham our father. This is the promise, “They will go out with great possessions,” and the spoils of the sea: preparation for the wisdom of Torah. Nevertheless, its root lay in external wisdom. Of Solomon it is said that his wisdom exceeded all the wisdom of Egypt—that is, their external wisdom. Solomon’s entire desire was for wisdom, and in his dream he asked only for this. His power was likewise fixed in his possessions; Shishak desired this, and it returned to its place. External wisdom was truly their portion, but it was lent temporarily to Israel so that through it the wisdom of the blessed God could be established in their hearts. This continued until King Solomon, who composed Proverbs to clarify the wisdom of Torah. Then they no longer needed external wisdom, and each thing returned to its place.
records.targetHebrew: וְזֶה שֶׁהוֹדִיעוּהוּ בְּכָאן גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, וּבַסּוֹף: "וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל", וְ"גָדוֹל" מוֹרֶה עַל מִדּוֹת עַתִּיקָא, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמְּקֻשָּׁרִין בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, וְזֶה הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם, שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ שָׁם עַל יְדֵי הָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת, שֶׁבְּכָל מַכָּה יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּדָּה אַחַת בַּקְּלִיפָּה, שֶׁיֵּשׁ גַּם כֵּן עֶשֶׂר זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה, וְנִכְנְסוּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה בְּמִדָּה אַחַת, עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, לו עַמּוּד א): "נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל".
records.targetEnglish: This is why he was informed here of the Egyptian exile and, at its end, “Afterward they will go out with great possessions.” “Great” indicates the qualities of Atika: being bound to the root. These are the great possessions they brought out of Egypt. Through the ten plagues they were clarified there in all ten qualities: in each plague Israel left one quality on the impure side, which also has ten corresponding qualities, and entered one quality in holiness. This resembles the holy Zohar’s expression, “Striking Egypt and healing Israel.”
records.themeTitle: The great possessions of Egypt include powers redirected into holiness
records.themeSummary: The ten plagues clarify qualities that had been held on the opposite side, giving spiritual content to the material departure from Egypt.
records.explanation: Lech Lecha explains the promised possessions through Israel’s movement from each impure quality into its holy counterpart. This develops the present siman’s claim that a people’s intense desire can become impressed upon its wealth. The possessions matter through the powers carried and redirected with them, especially the desire that becomes preparation for Torah’s wisdom. Their value cannot be reduced to an increase of property without that clarification.

records.originHebrew: עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא כְּלִי קִבּוּל לְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ. וְזֶהוּ תְּרוּמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן: "מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת כה, ב), דִּנְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא בִּנְיַן הַמִּשְׁכָּן דִּשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים. וּבָזֶה הוּא כָּל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַרְגָּשַׁת אֶחָד מִשְׁכַּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבּוֹ לַחֲבֵירוֹ; כִּי כְּפִי נְדִיבַת לְבָבוֹ בְּתִגְבּוֹרֶת חֶשְׁקוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג, כָּךְ הוּא שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.originEnglish: Through desire, a person becomes a vessel for the Divine Presence to dwell within his heart. This is the contribution for the Tabernacle: ‘From every person whose heart moves him.’ Through Israel’s generous heart the Tabernacle is built, the dwelling of the Divine Presence below. In this, each person is according to what he measures within his heart: one person’s awareness of God’s dwelling in his heart is unlike another’s. According to his heart’s generosity, in the strengthening of his desire to attain, so is the dwelling of the Divine Presence.
records.targetHebrew: וּבַחֲנֻכָּה מַדְלִיקִין שְׁמוֹנָה נֵרוֹת, כִּי הַנֵּר שְׁמִינִי מְרַמֵּז עַל בִּינָה לִבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת הָאוֹרוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים, וְהַיְנוּ הַתְּשׁוּקָה וְהָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְהַגִּיעַ לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁתִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּלֵּב. וְעִקַּר הַגַּעְגּוּעִים וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה בַּלֵּב לִזְכּוֹת לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה נִתְגַּלָּה אָז בִּימֵי גְּזֵרַת יָוָן, שֶׁהָיָה לְבַטְּלָם מִתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת; וְהָיָה לִבָּם נִשְׁבָּר מְאֹד מִזֶּה, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁמִּן הַשָּׁמַיִם מְעַכְּבִין מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם מְקֻבָּל בְּעֵינָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא דּוֹמֶה כְּשׁוֹפֵךְ קִיתוֹן עַל פָּנָיו (בְּסֻכָּה). וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְמַרְמְרוּ וְגָדְלָה הַתְּשׁוּקָה בְּלִבָּם לַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה בַּסֵּתֶר; וְגַם אוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ לְהַצְנִיעַ עַצְמָם וְלַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, עוֹד יוֹתֵר גָּדְלָה הַצְּעָקָה וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה בְּלִבָּם לִזְכּוֹת לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְנֵס שֶׁנִּזְדַּמֵּן לָהֶם הַשַּׁפּוּדִין שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַמְּנוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל לִמְאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַנֵּרוֹת, שֶׁהִיא כְּנֶגֶד הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה כְּלִי לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁפָּע בּוֹ מְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה.
records.targetEnglish: On Chanukah we light eight lamps. The eighth alludes to understanding in the heart, the source of the seven lights mentioned above: the heart’s longing and will to reach the illumination of Torah so that it spreads within the heart. The deepest yearning to attain Torah’s light was revealed in the days of the Greek decree, which sought to abolish Torah and commandments. Their hearts were greatly broken by this: it seemed that Heaven was preventing them because their Torah and commandments were not accepted before God, like a servant whose pitcher is poured back into his face. Through this they grew bitter and their hearts’ longing to study Torah in secret increased. Even those who could not hide themselves and study had an even greater cry and longing within their hearts to attain Torah’s light. Through this they merited the miracle of finding iron spits to make the menorah, the vessel receiving the light of the seven lamps. It corresponds to the will in the heart, through which a vessel is made to receive Torah’s illumination.
records.themeTitle: Longing for Torah can prepare a vessel even when its outward expression is obstructed
records.themeSummary: The iron spits used for the menorah give a physical image of a vessel formed through Israel’s intensified desire for Torah.
records.explanation: Chanukah describes both those able to learn in secret and those prevented from doing so, whose yearning nevertheless deepened. It relates the resulting menorah to the heart made ready to receive illumination. This gives a concrete example of the present siman’s opening: the willing heart is itself part of building a dwelling for the Shechinah. The siman then distinguishes this varied measure of positive reception from the equal foundation shared by all Israel.

records.originHebrew: עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא כְּלִי קִבּוּל לְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ. וְזֶהוּ תְּרוּמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן: "מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת כה, ב), דִּנְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא בִּנְיַן הַמִּשְׁכָּן דִּשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים. וּבָזֶה הוּא כָּל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַרְגָּשַׁת אֶחָד מִשְׁכַּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבּוֹ לַחֲבֵירוֹ; כִּי כְּפִי נְדִיבַת לְבָבוֹ בְּתִגְבּוֹרֶת חֶשְׁקוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג, כָּךְ הוּא שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.  וְיֵשׁ עוֹד תְּרוּמַת הָאֲדָנִים וּדְקָרְבָּנוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ: "הֶעָשִׁיר לֹא יַרְבֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוֹת ל, טו), שֶׁבֵּין הֶעָשִׁיר בְּדַעַת וּבְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב וְתִגְבּוֹרֶת הַחֵשֶׁק, וּבֵין הֶעָנִי – שָׁוִים בַּחֲלָקִים; כִּי הוּא "לְכַפֵּר עַל נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם" כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בַּכָּתוּב, וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד): דִּלְכַפֵּר אַעֵגֶל; פֵּירוּשׁ: לְקַנֵּחַ לִכְלוּךְ דְּחֶשְׁקוֹת רָעוֹת מִן הַלֵּב. וְכֵן בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פִּינְחָס): "תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר מְכַפֵּר וְכוּלֵי"; וּבְעִנְיַן הַרְחָקָה מִן הָרַע כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁוִים, שֶׁכֻּלָּם יוּכְלוּ לִינָּקוֹת מִן הָרַע בְּתַכְלִית, רַק חִלּוּק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת הוּא בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַטּוֹב.
records.originEnglish: Through yearning a person becomes a vessel for the indwelling of God’s presence within his heart. This is the contribution for the Mishkan, “From every person whose heart moves him”: through the generosity of Israel’s hearts the Mishkan is built, the dwelling of God in the lower realm. In this matter, each person experiences it according to the measure of his heart. One person’s sense of God dwelling within him is unlike another’s, for the indwelling corresponds to the generosity of his heart and the strength of his yearning to attain it. There is also the contribution for the sockets and for the offerings, concerning which it says, “The rich shall not give more.” The one rich in understanding, feeling of the heart, and strength of yearning, and the poor person, contribute equal portions, because it is “to atone for your lives,” as Scripture states. The Jerusalem Talmud, Shekalim, explains that it atones for the calf: that is, to cleanse the heart of the stain of evil desires. Likewise, concerning the communal offerings the Sages said that the morning daily offering atones. In distancing themselves from evil all Israel are equal, for all can become completely clean of evil; differences of degree concern the attainment of the good.
records.targetHebrew: וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעִיקַּר הַמְכוּוָּן בִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הָיָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עִיקַּר שְׁכִינָה בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים. וּבְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת נִתְעַלָּה וְיָשַׁב עַל כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדוֹ וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁקָּבַע שְׁכִינָתוֹ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים וְאָז עָשָׂה חֲנוּכָּה. וְכֵן חֲנוּכַּת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ. וְכֵן הָיָה חֲנוּכַּת הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ שֶׁכָּל א׳ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יַעֲשֶׂה חֲנוּכַּת הַבַּיִת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרֵךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְזֶה יְכוֹלִים לַעֲשׂוֹת בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה. וְזֶה קַיָּים לָעַד אַף בַּגָּלוּת וְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ. וְזֶה זֵכֶר לַחֲנוּכַּת הַמִּשְׁכָּן שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן בַּמִּדְבָּר בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ וְלֹא הָיָה קָבוּעַ בְּמָקוֹם רַק בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁחָנוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל קָבְעוּ מְקוֹמוֹ וְשָׁם הָיָה מִשְׁכַּן הַשְּׁכִינָה.
records.targetEnglish: The chief purpose in creating the world was that the Shekhinah should dwell primarily in the lower realm. On Shabbat He rose and sat upon His throne of glory: that is, He established His presence in the lower realm, and then held its dedication. The same applies to the dedication of the Mishkan and the Temple. Likewise, in the Hasmonean dedication they instituted that every Jew should dedicate a dwelling, for God dwells in the hearts of the children of Israel. This can be done “in those days, at this time.” It endures forever, even in exile and outside the Land of Israel. It commemorates the Mishkan’s dedication, which likewise took place in the wilderness, outside the Land. The Mishkan was not fixed in one location; wherever Israel encamped, they established its place, and there the divine presence dwelled.
records.themeTitle: The dedication of a dwelling in the heart remains possible in exile
records.themeSummary: Chanukah’s household dedication continues the Mishkan’s capacity to establish the Shechinah wherever Israel encamps.
records.explanation: Chanukah explains how the dwelling described in this siman is relevant beyond the original building of the Mishkan. Each person’s dedication of a house expresses the Shechinah’s dwelling in Jewish hearts, and this remains possible outside Eretz Yisrael and in exile. This preserves both dimensions of the siman: the divine purpose of dwelling below is shared, while the willing heart gives each person’s reception its particular measure and expression.

records.originHebrew: וְזֶה טַעַם בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי עַל יְדֵי מַלְכֵי פָּרַס, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרָכוֹת (ח:): "בְּשַׁבָּת הַפַּרְסִיִּים צְנוּעִים וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה נִיצוֹץ קָדוֹשׁ שֶׁלָּהֶם – מִדַּת הַצְּנִיעוּת; רַק דְּמַיְיתֵי עֲלָהּ תֵּיכֶף אַחַר כָּךְ: "אֵלּוּ פַּרְסִיִּים הַמְקוּדָּשִׁים לְגֵיהִנָּם", דְּאָסוּר לְסַפֵּר בְּשֶׁבַח עַכּוּ״ם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כ.). וּבֶאֱמֶת הֵם מַעֲלָתָם הִיא הַמְּבִיאָתַם לְגֵיהִנָּם, כִּי צְנִיעוּתָם הוּא כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאות תַּאֲוָתָם בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, וְגַם מִצַּד עַיִן הָרָע דִּצְרֵי עַיִן שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם, כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רנ"ה]. וְכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ כֹּחוֹ יוֹתֵר שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָאוּמָּה (מְגִילָּה יג.): "מִגְּנוּתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע אַתָּה לָמֵד שִׁבְחוֹ וְכוּלֵי", גַּם כֵּן בִּצְנִיעוּת, רַק שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִגְּנוּתוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּכַוָּנָתוֹ הַכֹּל לִגְנוּת. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם לְגַבֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא טוֹב, וְזָכְתָה אֶסְתֵּר, כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם עַמּוּד ב): "בִּשְׂכַר צְנִיעוּת שֶׁהָיְתָה וְכוּלֵי", וְהִיא קָלְטָה מִדַּת הַצְּנִיעוּת הַטּוֹבָה "הַצְנֵעַ לֶכֶת עִם אֱלֹהֶיךָ", שֶׁגַּם הִיא מִמִּדָּה זוֹ – לִהְיוֹת בְּהֶעְלֵם וְלֹא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת.
records.originEnglish: This is why the Second Temple was built through the kings of Persia. As is written in Berakhot 8b in praise of the Persians, “They are modest …”: this was their holy spark, the quality of modesty. But the Gemara immediately brings the statement, “These are the Persians consecrated for Gehinnom,” for it is forbidden to recount the praise of idolaters, as stated in Avodah Zarah 20a. In truth, their own excellence is what brings them to Gehinnom, because their modesty is for the purpose of satisfying their desire all the more, and also because of the evil eye and begrudging disposition they possessed, as explained above. Similarly, concerning Ahasuerus—whose royal power is greater because it encompasses the entire nation—the Sages say, “From the disgrace of that wicked man you learn his praise …,” also concerning modesty. But this is truly his disgrace, as above, since his intention is wholly disgraceful. Nevertheless, for Israel it is good. Esther merited it, as the Sages said, “In reward for the modesty that she possessed ….” She absorbed the good quality of modesty, “Walk modestly with your God,” which likewise means remaining concealed rather than revealed.
records.targetHebrew: וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן רֶמֶז מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אוֹהֵב אֲנִי אֶת הַפַּרְסִיִּים: הֵן צְנוּעִין בַּאֲכִילָתָן, וּצְנוּעִין בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא, וּצְנוּעִין בְּדָבָר אַחֵר", מִפְּנֵי שֶׁזֶּהוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ הַצְּנִיעוּת; רַק סָמוּךְ לָזֶה אָמְרוּ: "'אֲנִי צִוֵּיתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁי' אֵלּוּ הַפַּרְסִיִּים הַמְּקֻדָּשִׁין וּמְזֻמָּנִין לְגֵיהִנָּם", שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עִנְיָן זֶה הוּא קְדֻשָּׁה, הַגּוֹדֵר עַצְמוֹ בִּצְנִיעוּת, וְאֶצְלָם הוּא רַק עַל הַגַּוֶן וּמְקֻדָּשִׁים לְגֵיהִנָּם (וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר י״ד).
records.targetEnglish: This is also the hint in what is said in Berakhot 8b: “In three matters I love the Persians: they are modest in their eating, modest in the privy, and modest in another matter.” For this is the root of modesty. Yet close to it the Sages said, “‘I have commanded My consecrated ones’—these are the Persians, who are consecrated and prepared for Gehinnom.” Among Israel, this matter is holiness—restraining oneself in modesty—whereas among them it is only the outward appearance, and they are consecrated for Gehinnom. This was explained in discourse 14.
records.themeTitle: The holiness of modesty depends on what its concealment serves
records.themeSummary: An outwardly similar restraint can protect avodah or merely provide cover for a contrary desire.
records.explanation: Chanukah places the praise of Persian modesty beside its criticism and distinguishes the outward form from its inward purpose. This clarifies the precise extraction described in the present siman: Esther receives the holy quality of concealed service, rather than adopting the intention in which that quality had been clothed. The siman’s later discussion of her concealed holiness depends on this distinction between the appearance of an act and the direction of the heart within it.
